verdict.rationale: AgentMail documents a hosted MCP server that exposes inbox, message, thread, draft and attachment tools to any compatible client, and skills that work with Claude Code and Codex. That gives external agents a documented connection to read (search, threads), triage (labels, allow/block lists), draft and send mail end to end. The catch is that these are AgentMail-hosted inboxes created for agents. Nothing shows the agent operating a user's existing mailbox (e.g., Gmail or Outlook), though IMAP/SMTP lets a human use the AgentMail inbox in their own client. Missing for 10: evidence of connecting the user's existing personal mailbox, explicit ChatGPT client documentation, and independent hands-on corroboration of an end-to-end agent triage workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an external agent — Claude, ChatGPT, or my own — can read, triage, draft, and send my email end to end through a documented connection

citations.quote: AgentMail runs a hosted MCP server at `https://mcp.agentmail.to/mcp` that exposes inbox, message, thread, draft, attachment, and calendar tools
This works with Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, Codex, and other compatible agents
Full-text search finds Threads by keyword across the sender, recipients, subject, and message body, ranked by relevance.
Use `Labels` to track the state of a conversation.
An agent can create a `Draft` for a sensitive or important `Message`, which a human can then review and approve before it's sent.
To start a new conversation, you can send a Message from one of your inboxes.
It gives agents their own inboxes to send, receive, and act upon emails.
